deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 37-39): Grothendieck is building a purely combinatorial (1-dimensional) description of arrangements of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane, given as combinatorial maps ('cartes'). The basic local building block is a triple I of non-concurrent pseudo-lines. Three such lines cut RP^2 into the 'octaèdre gauche' (projective, or general, octahedron): the hemi-octahedron, with 3 vertices, 6 edges and 4 triangular faces. Its 1-skeleton is the 'graphe octaédral gauche': 3 vertices, with each pair joined by two edges. Previous page: for each vertex i, A_i is the 2-element set of edges not passing through i, namely the two segments of the i-th line, which is a Z/2-torsor. The 1-skeleton has 8 'triangles' (one edge chosen from each A_i), and an embedding as a hemi-octahedron selects one parity class of 4 of them. So the extra 2-dimensional information is exactly a trivialization of the Z/2-torsor ⊗_i A_i. This trivialization is what Grothendieck calls an 'orientation' of the octahedral graph (statement (16)).

This page comments on the commutative cube (17) of categories. It has three binary axes:
- top/bottom: oriented ('+') versus non-oriented objects;
- left/right: ordinary or spherical objects (octahedron on S^2, with graph K_{2,2,2}) versus general or projective objects (hemi-octahedron in RP^2);
- back/front: 2-dimensional configurations (maps) versus 1-dimensional marked configurations (graphs).

The claimed properties of the arrows are as follows.
- Top face: all four arrows are equivalences. For example, Aut(oct^+), the rotation group of the octahedron (≅ S_4), maps isomorphically onto Aut(hemi-octahedron) ≅ S_4.
- Bottom face: oct → gr.oct and gr.oct → gr.oct.g are equivalences. The arrow oct → oct.g is surjective on Hom, with kernel the antipodal map: 48 → 24. The arrow oct.g → gr.oct.g is faithful but not full: Aut of the hemi-octahedral graph is (Z/2)^3 ⋊ S_3 of order 48, while the hemi-octahedron has 24 automorphisms.
- Vertical arrows (forgetting orientation): all four are faithful.
- Left/right arrows: equivalences except oct → oct.g (surjective on Hom).
- Back/front arrows: equivalences except oct.g → gr.oct.g (faithful). This is precisely the defect that the orientation datum of (16) repairs.

The marginal note ('commencer à S̃_n ... S_n × {±1}') seems to flag a group-theoretic reformulation or generalization. The octahedral group is S_4 × {±1} ≅ W(B_3), as opposed to a nontrivial extension S̃_n. This suggests he contemplates n hyperplanes / n-dimensional cross-polytopes versus their projective quotients.

Purpose: the next page assembles these local data. An orientation of (K, (D_i)) is the choice, for every non-concurrent triple, of such a trivialization. He then claims that the functor 'arrangement ↦ (1-skeleton, pseudo-lines, orientation)' is fully faithful on isomorphisms. In other words, a combinatorial pseudo-line arrangement is recovered from its marked 1-skeleton plus one Z/2 datum per triple.
errors: The equivalence gr.oct → gr.oct.g cannot be the naive antipodal quotient of graphs. The antipodal automorphism of K_{2,2,2} induces the identity on the quotient graph, so that functor would not even be faithful. Commutativity of the cube with oct ≈ gr.oct and oct → oct.g killing ±1 is consistent only if the bottom-right equivalence is the abstract identification of the data (3-set I with a Z/2-torsor per element): pairs of opposite vertices of the octahedron ↔ the pairs A_i of opposite edges of the hemi-octahedral graph. The page does not make explicit which functor is meant.
The page is a summary of a diagram; the claims are stated without proof. They are easily checked by counting automorphism groups (48 / 24 / 48), and I found them consistent under the reading above.

ideas.what: Hemi-octahedron as the local model of three non-concurrent pseudo-lines in RP^2; its 1-skeleton with doubled edges; the 2-cell structure encoded by a trivialization of the Z/2-torsor ⊗A_i
ideas.modern_name: Local (triangle) data of a projective pseudo-line arrangement; reorientation-invariant rank-3 oriented matroid data; embedding of a graph as a map determined by a choice of face cycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pseudo-line arrangements: Levi 1926, Ringel 1956, Grünbaum 1972; Folkman–Lawrence 1978 (topological representation); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished Montpellier notes; the general theory of 'cartes' is evoked in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Commutative cube of categories (oriented/non-oriented × spherical/projective × 2-dim/1-dim marked), with each arrow classified as equivalence, faithful, or surjective on Hom
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of groupoids of maps and graphs; automorphism groups W(B_3) ≅ S_4 × Z/2 versus S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (regular polytopes / maps theory, e.g. Coxeter)

ideas.what: Reconstruction (full faithfulness on isomorphisms) of a combinatorial pseudo-line arrangement from its marked 1-skeleton plus a Z/2 'orientation' for each non-concurrent triple (stated on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Arrangements determined by triple data — analogue of chirotope / Folkman–Lawrence correspondence for unoriented pseudo-lines (reorientation classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence 1978; Bland–Las Vergnas 1978; Björner et al., 'Oriented Matroids' (1993)

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently encodes the 2-cell structure of a pseudo-line arrangement by Z/2-torsor trivializations indexed by triples of lines. This is a torsor-theoretic, reorientation-invariant counterpart of the chirotope of a rank-3 oriented matroid, apparently developed without reference to the oriented-matroid literature (Folkman–Lawrence, Las Vergnas) contemporaneous with it.
missed.quote: les quatre flèches de passage sont des équivalences sauf oct. g → gr. oct. généraux, qui est fidèle et fait l'objet de l'énoncé (16) plus haut.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest: it documents Grothendieck reinventing oriented-matroid-type encodings in a categorical/torsor language. The torsor formulation (orientation as trivialization of ⊗A_i) is a natural cohomological packaging not standard in the oriented-matroid literature. It is probably equivalent to known results, though.

missed.claim: The marginal note pointing to S̃_n versus S_n × {±1} suggests an intended generalization to n lines/hyperplanes, or to cross-polytopes and their projective quotients, with a group-theoretic description of automorphisms. It is not carried out on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: the higher-rank analogue (hyperplane pseudo-arrangements in RP^{n-1}, with local models given by hemi-cross-polytopes) is covered by oriented matroid theory. Any distinctive twist would lie only in the extension-class viewpoint, and the note is too fragmentary to judge.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but essentially elementary bookkeeping of functors between octahedra, hemi-octahedra and their graphs, oriented or not. The underlying mathematics (local triple data determine a pseudo-line arrangement) is close to known oriented-matroid results. Only the categorical/torsor packaging and the fact that Grothendieck worked on this are of historical note.
